faqs.q: What is the Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump used for?
faqs.a: The Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump is a balanced fixed-displacement vane pump of the V10 pattern, listed at 13.1 cm³/rev and up to 2,500 psi (172 bar). Vane pumps of this type run on older industrial machines, mobile power steering, refuse trucks and agricultural equipment; the full range is on the [vane pumps shelf](/c/hydraulic-vane-pumps).

faqs.q: How do I choose between the 29 part numbers of the Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump?
faqs.a: The 29 part numbers of the Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump differ by rotation, shaft length and, on some, outlet position: 17 clockwise (CW) and 12 anticlockwise (CCW), with rotation viewed from the shaft end. Examples are V101B4B1A20R, V101B4B1B20R, V101B4B1C20R; match rotation and shaft to the pump you are replacing, or quote the number from the old nameplate.

faqs.q: How many part numbers does the Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump come in?
faqs.a: The Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump is listed in 29 part numbers, from V101B4B1A20R to V101P4P3C20R in the size table, in 17 CW and 12 CCW rotation. Send the number from your old pump and we confirm the match before supply.

faqs.q: What flow does the Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump deliver?
faqs.a: At the 1,200 rpm rated speed in the table, a V10 pump of 13.1 cm³/rev delivers a theoretical 15.7 L/min, since flow is displacement times speed. Its maximum speed is 3,400 rpm; flow rises in proportion, but only if the inlet can feed the pump at that speed.

faqs.q: Which rotation and shaft options does the Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump have?
faqs.a: Rotation is viewed from the shaft end, and this listing has 17 clockwise (CW) and 12 anticlockwise (CCW). The shaft is a 3/4" straight keyed shaft in two lengths, 13 part numbers standard and 16 with the 1.75" extension, so check the old pump shaft before ordering.

faqs.q: What pressure and speed is the Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump rated for?
faqs.a: The Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump is rated up to 2,500 psi (172 bar) maximum pressure at a maximum speed of 3,400 rpm. The size table gives a rated speed of 1,200 rpm; Vickers publishes these V-series ratings on petroleum oil with 0 psi inlet, and they fall on fire-resistant fluids.

faqs.q: Which oil and inlet conditions suit the Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump?
faqs.a: Use anti-wear hydraulic oil at 13 to 54 cSt running viscosity. At its 3,400 rpm top speed the V10 13.1 cm³/rev ring draws about 44.5 L/min through the inlet, so keep the suction line short and inlet vacuum under 5 inHg, the Vickers limit on petroleum oil for V-series pumps.

faqs.q: What shaft coupling and drive does the Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump need?
faqs.a: The pump takes a 3/4" straight keyed shaft, so the coupling or flange must match that shaft and turn the pump in the right direction (CW is the main rotation here, V101P4P3C20R is one example). Drive sets and pump mounts are on the [power units and parts shelf](/c/hydraulic-power-units).

faqs.q: How is the Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump serviced or rebuilt?
faqs.a: A worn V10 13.1 cm³/rev pump is usually repaired by changing its cartridge (rotor, vanes, ring and side plates) in the existing body, and rotation is changed by reassembling the internal parts. At 172 bar working pressure the cleanliness target is ISO 4406 19/17/14, and the [vane pump guide for V10, V20 and T6](/blog/vane-pump-guide-v10-v20-t6) covers the steps.

faqs.q: Which machines typically use the Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump?
faqs.a: V10 pumps are fitted where a quiet, smooth flow is wanted, such as industrial machines, mobile power steering, refuse trucks and agricultural equipment; at 13.1 cm³/rev this one suits circuits needing about 15.7 L/min at 1,200 rpm. For more than 2,500 psi from a vane pump, the Parker T6 and T7 families in the [vane pump guide for V10, V20 and T6](/blog/vane-pump-guide-v10-v20-t6) are the usual step up.

faqs.q: How does the Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump compare with the 16.4 cm³/rev V10?
faqs.a: The Fluidyne V10 13.1 cm³/rev vane pump gives less flow per revolution than the [16.4 cm³/rev pump](/p/fluidyne-v10-vane-pumps-16-4-cm-rev), and its maximum speed is 3,400 rpm against 3,200 rpm. Both are rated up to 2,500 psi, so pick the displacement from the flow you need at your running speed.

faqs.q: Which oil and inlet conditions suit the Fluidyne V20 29.7 cm³/rev vane pump?
faqs.a: Use anti-wear hydraulic oil at 13 to 54 cSt running viscosity. At its 3,000 rpm top speed the V20 29.7 cm³/rev ring draws about 89.1 L/min through the inlet, so keep the suction line short and inlet vacuum under 5 inHg, the Vickers limit on petroleum oil for V-series pumps.

faqs.q: How is the Fluidyne V20 29.7 cm³/rev vane pump serviced or rebuilt?
faqs.a: A worn V20 29.7 cm³/rev pump is usually repaired by changing its cartridge (rotor, vanes, ring and side plates) in the existing body, and rotation is changed by reassembling the internal parts. At 172 bar working pressure the cleanliness target is ISO 4406 19/17/14, and the [vane pump guide for V10, V20 and T6](/blog/vane-pump-guide-v10-v20-t6) covers the steps.
